The most defensible packet preserves launch velocity by certifying on aggregate readiness while explicitly disclosing the unresolved small-business support weakness and noting follow-up confirmation due to sampling uncertainty.

Under the stated certification policy, aggregate readiness can support launch, but subgroup weaknesses are not erased and must be disclosed when material. The small-business support slice is below both its warning and preferred thresholds, so certification should be issued with explicit model-card disclosure of that slice weakness and with a stated plan to confirm performance in the next evaluation batch given the wider confidence interval.
